name: Temporal Noise Pattern
description: Isolates and characterizes temporal noise signatures by comparing frame-to-frame noise correlation against sensor-specific noise models, revealing the absence of authentic electronic readout noise in synthesized video.
algorithm: Temporal Noise Pattern — Statistical Pattern Analyzer
mechanism:
This method analyzes temporal noise patterns for video deepfake detection:

1. **Temporal Noise Extraction**: The temporal noise component is extracted by computing per-pixel temporal variance in static regions. This isolates noise from signal, capturing the stochastic temporal fluctuation characteristics of the imaging system.

2. **Noise Model Identification**: Camera temporal noise follows specific models: (a) photon shot noise (Poisson, signal-dependent), (b) read noise (Gaussian, signal-independent), (c) thermal noise (dark current). The method fits these physical noise models to the observed temporal noise. AI-generated video typically doesn't follow physical camera noise models.

3. **Noise Spatial Homogeneity**: Camera noise is spatially homogeneous (same sensor for all pixels) with possible variation from vignetting. The method checks noise spatial distribution — deepfakes show different noise characteristics in generated face regions (from the generator's stochastic process) vs. captured background (from camera noise).

4. **Noise-Signal Dependency**: In camera-captured video, noise variance depends on signal level (shot noise ∝ signal). The method checks this dependency — AI-generated noise may be signal-independent (additive noise model) or show incorrect signal-noise relationship.

5. **Temporal Noise Correlation**: Camera temporal noise is temporally uncorrelated (white). The method checks temporal autocorrelation of the noise signal — AI-generated temporal noise may show temporal correlations from the generation process (autoregressive generation, frame interpolation), producing non-white temporal noise distinguishable from camera noise.
parameters:
Analysis type: statistical
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through temporal noise pattern analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
